search_log: Searched "James A. Michener Poland novel excerpt first chapter", "Poland point of view narrator third person", Google Books previews, and chapter-structure terms.
Opened the BookRags point-of-view section, which explicitly describes whole-book third-person narration.
Checked Penguin Random House's edition page and Read Sample offering; the accessible page exposed catalog copy but not sample prose.

Checked Google Books, Open Library, and Internet Archive records; previews were limited or access-restricted and yielded no inspectable Tier A prose. Unofficial OCR/PDF copies were excluded from evidentiary use.
Searched "James Michener Poland analysis narration narrator omniscient" and related phrases; weaker automated summaries echoed an omniscient narrator but were not needed for the decision.

Opened the Washington Post contemporary review to verify the modern frame and historical-section structure; it did not explicitly state narrative person. No source indicated alternating or participating base narration.
person_note: The diagnostic quotations repeatedly show a nonparticipating narrator recounting characters' actions, perceptions, and historical circumstances in third person, including both scene narration and broad authorial exposition. First- and second-person forms occur only in dialogue, gnomic commentary, paratext, or an embedded joke. The explicit whole-book BookRags description agrees and no researched source reports alternating narration. Confidence is medium because the accessible web evidence included no sustained authorized prose excerpt or Tier B structural study.
